title: Projective representation theory of spin space groups
authors: Zheng Zhang, Peiyuan Wang, Y. X. Zhao
abstract: Spin space groups provide the natural symmetry framework for magnetic crystals with weak spin-orbit coupling, but extracting their physical consequences requires a general theory of irreducible representations. The central difficulty is that spin space groups are represented projectively: their factor systems can render lattice translations noncommuting, induce nonsymmorphic actions in momentum space, and modify the projective structure of little cogroups. These effects lie beyond conventional space-group and double-group representation theory. Here, using Mackey's theory of group extensions, we develop a unified constructive framework for all collinear, coplanar, and noncoplanar spin space groups, including antiunitary symmetries and general factor systems. A central technical result is a canonical decomposition of the relevant factor system $ν$ into a translational factor $σ$, a mixed factor $γ$ coupling translations to point-group operations, and a point-group factor $α$. This decomposition makes transparent how ordinary representation theory is modified: $σ$ determines the projective translation algebra and the appropriate Brillouin zone, $γ$ controls the momentum-space group action and can make it nonsymmorphic, and $α$ contributes to the factor systems of little cogroups. On this basis, we construct all projective irreducible corepresentations by induction over momentum-space orbits. The framework identifies which nonsymmorphic momentum-space symmetries can be realized by spin space groups and reveals Brillouin spaces that are compact flat manifolds rather than tori, symmetry-enforced Zak phases, reconstructed high-symmetry momenta and band degeneracies, and new types of quasiparticles. Our results establish the representation-theoretic foundation for systematic studies of weak-spin-orbit-coupled magnetic materials.
summary: This work establishes a comprehensive representation-theoretic foundation for studying magnetic crystals by developing a unified theory for Spin Space Groups. It tackles the mathematical difficulty posed by the projective nature of these symmetries using an extended Mackey theory. The resulting framework predicts novel physical consequences, such as modified Brillouin zones and symmetry-enforced topological phases, for weak spin-orbit coupling materials.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for a general, unified representation theory for Spin Space Groups (SSGs) because their projective nature complicates standard group and double-group representation methods.
main_result: The authors develop a canonical decomposition of the magnetic factor system into translational, mixed, and point-group factors, allowing for the construction of all projective irreducible corepresentations for various SSG classes.
method: The theory employs Mackey's theory of group extensions, extending it to handle antiunitary symmetries and developing a systematic framework based on the decomposition of the factor system.
model_or_system: The theory applies to magnetic crystals characterized by weak spin-orbit coupling, using the SSG as the fundamental symmetry framework for describing their electronic and magnetic properties.
key_observables: Symmetry-enforced Zak phases, reconstructed high-symmetry momenta, and the identification of new types of quasiparticles.

main_assumptions: The central assumption is that the physical symmetries can be systematically classified and analyzed by extending Mackey's theory to account for the projective nature of the spin operations.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the group structure of SSGs, develops the theory in two stages (projective corepresentations of the quotient group, then the full SSG), and finally derives physical consequences regarding symmetry constraints and Brillouin spaces.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter symmetry, the rigorous development of projective representation theory and group extensions provides powerful mathematical tools applicable to any system where symmetries are described by non-trivial factor systems, including those studied in quantum optics or AMO physics.
